Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, it is We who give life and cause death, and to Us is the final return.﴾

We have already discussed in Surah Yasin what relates to His words ﴿Indeed, it is We﴾. As for His words ﴿give life and cause death﴾, the meaning of "giving life" is the first giving of life, and ﴿cause death﴾ refers to the first death. His words ﴿and to Us﴾ explain the gathering (hashr). He placed ﴿Indeed, it is We﴾ first to define His greatness; a speaker says "I, I" meaning that he is well known. And ﴿give life and cause death﴾ are matters that confirm the meaning of greatness. ﴿And to Us is the final return﴾ is the explanation of the intended meaning.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 50, verses 44–45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿On the Day the earth splits asunder from them, hastening⟩. The governing element (al-'amil) in it is what is in His saying: ﴿the Day of emergence⟩ [Qaf: 42], from the verb, meaning: they will come forth ﴿on the Day the earth splits asunder from them, hastening﴾. And His saying: ﴿hastening﴾ (sira'an) is a circumstantial state (hal) of those who come forth, because His saying, exalted is He: ("from them") indicates that they are the ones acted upon by the splitting. So the splitting occurs at the moment of emerging from the grave, just as one says "he uncovered it (kashafa 'anhu)", so it is "uncovered from him" (maksuf 'anhu). Thus "sira'an" takes the form of the passive participle, as if He said: hastening. And sira' is the plural of sari', like kiram, the plural of karim.

His saying: ﴿That is a gathering⟩ may refer to the splitting from them, or it may refer to the bringing forth indicated by His saying "hastening", or its meaning may be: that gathering is an easy gathering, since the gathering has been known from the expressions that came before.

His saying, exalted is He: ("upon Us it is easy") with the placing of the adverbial phrase first indicates exclusivity, meaning: it is easy for Us, not for other than Us. This is a response to their saying: ﴿That is a distant return⟩ [Qaf: 3]. Gathering (al-hashr) is assembling. The Day of Resurrection is the assembling of parts with one another, the assembling of spirits with bodies, meaning that each spirit is joined with its body, and the assembling of scattered peoples and dispersed remains, and all of this is one in the act of gathering.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿We know best what they say, and you are not over them a compeller. So remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning⟩. In it there are aspects.

One: It is a consolation to the heart of the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers, and an exhortation to them regarding what the Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded to do of patience and glorification, meaning: occupy yourself with what We have said and let not complaint to Us distract you, for We know their words and see their deeds. On this view, His saying: ﴿and you are not over them a compeller⟩ fits it, meaning: do not say, "I was sent to them to guide them, so how shall I occupy myself with what distracts me from guidance, which is prayer and glorification?" For you were not sent to have power over their motives and capacities; you were only commanded to convey, and you have conveyed, so be patient, glorify, and await the Day on which the matter between you will be decided.

Two: It is a word of threat and warning, because His saying: ﴿and to Us is the final return⟩ is clearly a threat by the knowledge of your deeds, for whoever knows that his return is to the King, yet believes the King does not know what he does, does not refrain from vices; but if he knows that He knows it, and with Him is its unseen and to Him is its return, he refrains.

So He said: ﴿and to Us is the final return⟩ and ﴿We know best⟩, which is clearly a threat. This is then like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then to Us is your return, and We will inform you of what you used to do⟩ [Yunus: 23], ﴿Indeed He is Knower of what is within the breasts⟩.

Three: It is an affirmation of the gathering. When He made clear that the gathering is easy for Him, due to the perfection of His power and the executing of His will, yet its completion requires comprehensive knowledge, so that He distinguishes between a part of one body and a part of another body, the part of Zayd's body and the part of 'Amr's body, He said: ﴿That is a gathering upon Us, easy⟩ due to the perfection of Our power, and parts are not hidden from Us because of Our knowledge. On this view, His saying: ﴿We know best what they say⟩ means: We know the very thing they say in their saying: ﴿When we are dead and have become dust?⟩ [Qaf: 3] ﴿When we are lost in the earth?⟩ [al-Sajdah: 10], so He says: We know the parts of which they say that they are lost and hidden, and the meaning is not merely "We know what they say." And their saying in the first case may be that "ma" is a verbal-masdar (ma masdariyya), so that what is meant by His saying "ma yaqulun" is their saying; and in the other aspect it is a relative/informative "ma" (khabariyya). On this proof, His saying "We know best" is not valid, since there is no one who knows those parts besides Him so that He would say "We know best." We say: the answer to this has been known many times, from several aspects:

One: that the form af'al (comparative) does not require sharing in the basic act, as in His saying: ﴿And God is more worthy that you fear Him⟩ [al-Ahzab: 37], and in His saying: ﴿And better in appearance⟩ [Maryam: 77], and in His saying: ﴿And it is easier for Him⟩ [al-Rum: 27].

Two: its meaning is: We know best what they say, from every knower in respect of what he knows. The first is more correct, clearer, more evident, and better known.

His saying: (﴿and you are not over them a compeller⟩) has aspects:

One: that it is also a consolation. For when He bestowed upon him occupation with the otherworldly task, which is worship, He informed him that he was not diverted from the other task, which is raising the dead, just as when a king commands one of his servants with two tasks, and he shows incapacity in one of them, the king says to him: Turn to the other of the two, and We shall send one who can do what you were unable to do. So He said: "be patient and glorify, and you are not ... a compeller," meaning: their refusal was not due to any tyranny or arrogance on your part, so that they recoiled from the badness of your character; rather you were gentle with them, compassionate to them, you exerted yourself and conveyed, and they refused. So turn to patience and glorification, not diverted from the first task by reason of your tyranny. This is in the sense of His saying: ﴿You are not, by the grace of your Lord, a madman⟩, up to His saying: ﴿And indeed you are upon a tremendous character⟩ [al-Qalam: 2–4].

Two: it is a statement that the Prophet (ﷺ) brought what was incumbent upon him of guidance, for He sent him as a warner and guide, not as one who compels or forces. This is like His saying: ﴿We did not send you as a watcher over them⟩ [al-Nisa: 80], meaning: you guard them from disbelief and the Fire. And His saying: ﴿and you are not over them⟩ is in the sense of someone's saying: "Today so-and-so is over us," in answer to one who asks: "Who is over you today?", meaning: who is the governor over you?

Three: it is a statement that the time of the descent of the punishment has not yet come, for when the Prophet (ﷺ) warned and gave excuse and made it manifest, and they did not believe, he would say: this is the time of punishment. So He said: We know best what they say, and you are not over them one who has power, so remind of My punishment if they do not believe, those among them whom you know will believe, then exercise authority. This is supported by the statement of the exegetes that the verse was revealed before the revelation of the verse on fighting. On this view, His saying: ﴿so remind by the Qur'an whoever fears My warning⟩ means: those among them who remain, who fear the Day of warning.

There are other aspects:

One: We have explained in one aspect that His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So be patient over what they say and glorify⟩ [Qaf: 39] means: turn to worship. Then He said: and do not abandon guidance entirely, but ﴿remind⟩ [al-Dhariyat: 55] the believers, ﴿for the reminder benefits the believers⟩ [al-Dhariyat: 55], ﴿and turn away from the ignorant⟩. And His saying: ﴿by the Qur'an⟩ has aspects:

The first: remind by what is in the Qur'an, and recite the Qur'an to them, so that through what it contains of benefit they attain it.

The second: ﴿so remind by the Qur'an⟩, meaning: make clear by it that you are a messenger, since it is miraculous, and when your being a messenger is established, they are bound to accept your word in all that you say.

The third: the meaning is: remind in accordance with what is in the Qur'an of the commands given concerning conveyance and reminding, and then the Qur'an serves the Prophet's (ﷺ) benefit by it, meaning: make the Qur'an your leader, and remind them of what you were informed of in it, by reminding them. On the first, the meaning is: recite the Qur'an to them so that they may be reminded through it.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿whoever fears My warning⟩ is among what shows that fear (khashyah) indicates the greatness of the one feared more than fear (khawf) does, where He said "yakhafu" when He made the object of fear His punishment and warning, and He said: ﴿and fear Me⟩ [al-Baqarah: 150] when He made the object of fear His own great Self. In this verse there is an allusion to the three foundations (usul). His saying "remind" is an allusion to the fact that he is a sent one, commanded to remind, upon whom the Qur'an was revealed, as He said: "by the Qur'an." His saying "warning" (wa'id) is an allusion to the Last Day. The first-person pronoun in His saying "My warning" indicates oneness, for if He had said "whoever fears the warning of God," the mind would have gone off to every direction, in which the name God is shared; so He said "My warning," and the speaker is the most definite of definites and furthest from association with Him and from accepting sharing in Him. We have explained at the beginning of the surah that the beginning of the surah and its end are close in meaning, where He said at the beginning: ﴿Qaf. By the glorious Qur'an⟩ [Qaf: 1], and said at its end: ﴿so remind by the Qur'an⟩.

This is the end of the exegesis of this surah, and praise be to God, Lord of the worlds, and His blessings upon the seal of the Prophets and master of the Messengers, Muhammad the Prophet, and his family, companions, wives, and all his offspring.
